title: KV bucketed churn controller and granular GPU swap plan
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Implement a bucketed churn controller for the paged/blocked KV cache to reduce noisy eviction-induced OOMs and stabilize continuous batching throughput. This ticket covers a) a runtime admission controller that groups KV entries into churn buckets by recent access frequency and write intensity, b) a swap/hand-off protocol to drive deterministic GPU->host staging for low-value buckets, and c) integration points so the continuous batcher can hint hot-token affinity to avoid thrashing during high-concurrency spikes.
technical_spec:
Background: Our paged KV design divides model KV into fixed-size blocks that can be resident on GPU or evicted to host memory. Under workloads with high concurrency and variable sequence lengths, we observe repeated eviction/restore cycles for semantic hotset boundaries, causing elevated tail latency and OOMs when the batcher schedules many long-context requests concurrently.

Design overview:
1) Bucketed churn controller: maintain a small in-memory catalog of buckets. Each bucket is a logical grouping of blocks by (model, layer-range, token-offset quantile) and a churn score computed as an EWMA of eviction frequency, accessed-by-current-batcher-ratio, and recent read amplification. Buckets have states: HOT, WARM, COOL, and STAGED. Transitions based on thresholded churn_score and residency budget.
2) Deterministic swap hand-off: when a bucket becomes STAGED, initiate an ordered async transfer of associated blocks from GPU to host using the GPU DMA/peer-copy path. Each hand-off creates a short-lived lease token written to the resident-set catalog so inflight batchers can complete with local pinning; new requests will get a fallback placement to alternative model variant or a degraded latency path.
3) Batcher integration: the batcher exposes a token-affinity hint so requests referencing recently-used keys are co-scheduled in a small affinity window. The churn controller can increase affinity window size for HOT buckets and shrink it for WARM/COOL to reduce cross-request eviction pressure.
4) Paging heuristics: implement watermark-driven backpressure — when resident GPU memory crosses a high water mark, mark low-priority buckets for STAGED state, and throttle scheduling of non-affine requests until transfer completes.
5) Metrics & safety: add counters and histograms for per-bucket eviction_rate, restore_latency, staged_transfers_inflight, and pin_failures. Include a conservative fallback that delays host transfer if the number of pinned blocks across all buckets exceeds a configured safety_budget.

Trade-offs considered: aggressive bucketing reduces tail by keeping hot slices resident but risks underutilizing GPU if buckets are too narrow. Deterministic staging reduces unexpected OOMs but may increase host IO. We favor gradual transitions and safety budgets to avoid sudden degradation.
acceptance_criteria: Per-bucket churn_score implemented and persisted to runtime catalog
Deterministic async GPU->host hand-off for staged buckets with lease tokens and pin semantics
Batcher token-affinity API implemented and used to co-schedule hot requests in at least one path
Resident-set high/low watermark triggering and backpressure implemented
Automated tests covering bucket state transitions and staged handoff retry semantics
Performance: 99th percentile token latency reduced by >=15% under the long-tail synthetic workload (see test harness), and OOM incidence reduced to <1 per 1M requests in the stress test
Dashboard with per-bucket metrics (eviction_rate, restore_latency, staged_count) added to Console-facing runtime dashboard
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (2w): Add bucket catalog schema, churn_score calculation, and unit tests for transition logic
Phase 2 (2w): Implement deterministic staged hand-off path with lease tokens and host transfer shim; add integration tests in staging cluster
Phase 3 (1w): Add batcher token-affinity hint surface and a scheduler patch to co-locate affine requests
Phase 4 (1w): Implement watermarks, safety_budget enforcement, and backpressure hooks in admission controller
Phase 5 (1w): Instrumentation, dashboarding, and e2e performance validation with synthetic and captured production traces
Phase 6 (1w): Canary rollout and iterative tuning, rollback path ready
testing_plan: Unit tests for churn_score state machine and boundary conditions
Integration tests for staged handoff with simulated host IO failures and retries
Load test with mixed short/long-contexts to measure 50/95/99 percentiles and compare baseline vs change
Chaos test: kill transfer threads during staged transfer to ensure lease semantics avoid double-free/pin leaks
Canary in dedicated cluster with 100qps long-tail workload for 48 hours
risks: Increased host IO could saturate PCIe on older nodes leading to higher tail latency
Affinity window may create hotspots and reduce aggregate throughput if misconfigured
Lease token leaks could prevent reclamation and cause gradual OOMs
Backpressure may interact poorly with autoscaler leading to underprovisioning in bursts
rollback_plan: Feature flag to disable bucketed churn controller and revert to existing LRU-style eviction
Abort in-flight staged transfers and convert staged buckets back to WARM with immediate restore when toggled off
Fallback routing to lower-capacity model variant for affected customer tenants during rollback window
Post-rollback runbook: run resident-set scan and reconcile leaked pins
security_and_compliance: No plaintext customer data moved during host staging; transfers occur within same VPC and use existing KMS-wrapped keys for host-side swap artifacts. Coordinate with security for review if host-staging touches encrypted swap files (flagged false currently).
notes: Prototype in an earlier spike showed a 40% reduction in steady-state eviction churn for a single model with 32k contexts. This ticket generalizes the concept and hardens safety. Keep bucket cardinality bounded to avoid catalog blowup.
